relevance_reason: Reports 33 GGM patients from an Old Order Amish pedigree with homozygous SLC5A1 missense mutations co-segregating with disease.

findings.statement: Xin and Wang (2011) reported 33 patients with glucose-galactose malabsorption from a large Old Order Amish pedigree. All affected individuals presented with classic watery diarrhea and dehydration; increased bowel sounds, distended abdomen, vigorous nursing despite illness, and irritability and apathy were also noted at initial presentation.
quotes: Here, we report 33 patients with GGM from a large Old Order Amish pedigree and the associated mutations in SLC5A1 gene.
Clinically, all affected individuals presented with classic watery diarrhea and dehydration.
The increased bowel sounds, distended abdomen, vigorous nursing regardless of their illness, and irritability and apathy were also noted as part of the initial presentation.

findings.statement: Xin and Wang (2011) observed that patients who were correctly diagnosed and adequately managed showed immediate cessation of diarrhea and rapid rehydration, followed by normal growth and development, whereas a prolonged clinical course followed if the disease was not recognized.
quotes: Patients underwent a dramatic turnaround with an immediate cease of the diarrhea and a quick rehydration if they were correctly diagnosed and adequately managed, followed by a normal growth and development pattern afterwards; whereas a prolonged clinical course would follow if the disease was not recognized.

findings.statement: In 33 Old Order Amish patients with GGM, Xin and Wang (2011) sequenced the 15 protein-coding exons and exon-intron boundaries of SLC5A1 and identified homozygosity for four missense mutations, including c.152A>G (p.N51S), which co-segregated with the phenotype in all affected individuals.
quotes: Sequence analysis of the 15 protein-coding exons and the corresponding exon-intron boundaries of SLC5A1 gene revealed four homozygous missense mutations, c.152A>G (p.N51S), c.1231G>A (p.A411T), c.1673G>A (p.R558H), and c.1845C>G (p.H615Q), that co-segregate with the GGM phenotype in all of the affected individuals.

findings.statement: Xin and Wang (2011) identified a homozygous c.1231G>A (p.A411T) missense mutation in SLC5A1, one of four homozygous missense variants co-segregating with GGM in all 33 affected Old Order Amish individuals.
quotes: Sequence analysis of the 15 protein-coding exons and the corresponding exon-intron boundaries of SLC5A1 gene revealed four homozygous missense mutations, c.152A>G (p.N51S), c.1231G>A (p.A411T), c.1673G>A (p.R558H), and c.1845C>G (p.H615Q), that co-segregate with the GGM phenotype in all of the affected individuals.

findings.statement: Xin and Wang (2011) identified a homozygous c.1673G>A (p.R558H) missense mutation in SLC5A1, one of four homozygous missense variants co-segregating with GGM in all 33 affected Old Order Amish individuals.
quotes: Sequence analysis of the 15 protein-coding exons and the corresponding exon-intron boundaries of SLC5A1 gene revealed four homozygous missense mutations, c.152A>G (p.N51S), c.1231G>A (p.A411T), c.1673G>A (p.R558H), and c.1845C>G (p.H615Q), that co-segregate with the GGM phenotype in all of the affected individuals.

quotes: Sequence analysis of the 15 protein-coding exons and the corresponding exon-intron boundaries of SLC5A1 gene revealed four homozygous missense mutations, c.152A>G (p.N51S), c.1231G>A (p.A411T), c.1673G>A (p.R558H), and c.1845C>G (p.H615Q), that co-segregate with the GGM phenotype in all of the affected individuals.

findings.statement: Xin and Wang (2011) suggested a founder effect for the SLC5A1 mutations associated with GGM in the Amish and proposed population-specific genetic testing to allow early diagnosis, which they considered critical for a favorable outcome.
quotes: These findings suggest that founder effect of the SLC5A1 mutations associated with the disease in Amish and a population specific genetic testing is in need to pursue an early diagnosis which is critical for a favorable outcome.

relevance_reason: Case series of 8 Arab children with congenital glucose-galactose malabsorption, describing clinical features, diagnosis and response to treatment.

findings.statement: Abdullah et al. (1996) described 8 children from 8 different families with glucose-galactose malabsorption; 6 were Saudi Arabs and 2 were of other Arab nationalities. Mean age at presentation was 10.6 months, and the children had chronic watery diarrhea present since birth and failure to thrive. One child had a renal stone at the first visit, and another was found to have one on follow-up.
quotes: Eight children with chronic diarrhea from glucose-galactose malabsorption from eight different families are presented. Six children are Saudi Arabs and two are of the other Arab nationalities.
They were first seen for chronic watery diarrhea, present since birth, and failure to thrive.
One child had a renal stone at the first visit, and another was discovered to have one on follow-up.

findings.statement: Abdullah et al. (1996) confirmed the diagnosis of glucose-galactose malabsorption with laboratory tests, including small-bowel biopsy, histology, and small-bowel enzyme assay.
quotes: Laboratory investigations, including small-bowel biopsy, histology, and small-bowel enzyme assay, confirmed the diagnosis of glucose-galactose malabsorption.

findings.statement: Abdullah et al. (1996) reported that all 8 children with glucose-galactose malabsorption responded clinically to a fructose-based formula and were thriving at follow-up.
quotes: All the children responded clinically to fructose-based formula, and they are thriving at follow-up.

relevance_reason: Reports prenatal molecular diagnosis for GGM using the SGLT1 D28N mutation in a consanguineous family; adds diagnostic evidence.

findings.statement: Martín et al. (1996) performed prenatal screening for GGM in 2 subsequent pregnancies in a large consanguineous family in which 2 proband sibs with GGM had a missense mutation (D28N) in SGLT1. Exon 1 of SGLT1 was PCR-amplified from fetal genomic DNA and screened for D28N by EcoRV restriction digestion; the proband's sib was heterozygous and a cousin was not a carrier. Both children remained healthy without diarrheal symptoms at 2 years of age.
quotes: Prenatal screening for GGM was performed in two subsequent pregnancies in this large consanguineous family.
The first exon of the SGLT1 gene was PCR-amplified from genomic DNA and screened for the presence of the D28N mutation by EcoRV restriction digestion.
The proband's sibling was heterozygous and a cousin was not a carrier of the D28N mutation. Both children at 2-years of age remain healthy and have had no diarrhoeal symptoms.

relevance_reason: This paper screened SGLT1 in 30 patients with GGM and expressed the mutations to link them to the phenotype. Only the abstract was available.

findings.statement: Martín et al. (1996) stated that glucose-galactose malabsorption (GGM) is caused by a defect in the intestinal brush border Na+/glucose cotransporter SGLT1. The disorder presents in the neonatal period with diarrhea, which is fatal unless glucose and galactose are removed from the diet.
quotes: Glucose-Galactose Malabsorption (GGM) is caused by a defect in SGLT1. The phenotype is neonatal onset of diarrhea that results in death unless these sugars are removed from the diet.

findings.statement: Martín et al. (1996) screened the SGLT1 gene in 30 new patients with GGM. They used a heterologous expression system to link the mutations to the phenotype, and concluded that defects in SGLT1 trafficking and function cause the disorder.
quotes: The gene has now been screened in 30 new patients, and a heterologous expression system has been used to link the mutations to the phenotype.
Defects in Na+/glucose cotransporter (SGLT1) trafficking and function cause glucose-galactose malabsorption.

relevance_reason: Refines the chromosomal location of SGLT1, the gene whose mutation causes GGM, to 22q13.1 by FISH; also mentions the Asp28Asn missense mutation found in GGM patients.

findings.statement: Turk et al. (1993) used fluorescence in situ hybridization with a cosmid probe to refine the localization of the SGLT1 gene, which encodes the intestinal Na+/glucose cotransporter, from the distal long arm of chromosome 22 (22q11.2-qter) to 22q13.1.
quotes: The SGLT1 gene was previously shown to reside on the distal q arm of chromosome 22 (11.2-->qter). We have used a cosmid probe for fluorescence in situ hybridization, which refines the localization to 22q13.1

findings.statement: Turk et al. (1993) noted that in 2 patients with autosomal recessive glucose/galactose malabsorption, the cause was a missense mutation in SGLT1, asp28-to-asn (D28N), which was shown in vitro to eliminate SGLT1 transport activity.
quotes: In two patients with the autosomal recessive disease glucose/galactose malabsorption, the underlying cause was found to be a missense mutation in SGLT1, and the Asp28-->Asn change was demonstrated in vitro to eliminate SGLT1 transport activity.

relevance_reason: Reports a patient with congenital glucose-galactose malabsorption and her family. Includes studies of intestinal and renal glucose transport, detection of heterozygotes, and conclusions about inheritance.

findings.statement: Elsas et al. (1970) studied a 3-year-old girl with congenital glucose-galactose malabsorption. In vitro, her jejunal mucosa could not concentrate glucose at any point in a 60-minute incubation. Renal glucose titration showed a partial defect in renal glucose reabsorption.
quotes: Glucose transport by jejunal mucosa in vitro and kidney in vivo was investigated in a 3 yr old patient with congenital glucose-galactose malabsorption, her family, and 16 normal volunteers.
The proband's mucosa was unable to concentrate glucose throughout a 60 min incubation period.
A partial defect in renal glucose reabsorption was found in the proband.

phenotypes.text: partial defect in renal glucose reabsorption

findings.statement: Elsas et al. (1970) found that normal human jejunal mucosa transported glucose against a concentration gradient; transport was saturable, depended on sodium and energy, and showed competitive inhibition. Mucosa from 6 normal controls and from the proband's asymptomatic 5-year-old brother concentrated glucose to 16 times the medium concentration. Fructose was accumulated similarly in all subjects.
quotes: Glucose transport by normal human jejunal mucosa was concentrative, saturable, sodium and energy dependent, and exhibited competitive inhibition.
Biopsy specimens from six normal controls and an asymptomatic 5 yr old brother of the proband accumulated glucose to concentrations 16 times that in the incubation medium.
All subjects accumulated fructose similarly.

findings.statement: Elsas et al. (1970) found impaired intestinal glucose transport in both parents and a half sister of the proband, with values between those of normal controls and the proband. In these heterozygotes, glucose influx was impaired while efflux was the same as in controls. Kinetic analysis showed a reduced capacity (Vmax) with normal affinity (Km), and the authors concluded that heterozygotes can be detected.
quotes: Both of her parents and a half sister demonstrated impaired glucose transport. Their values fell between normal and those of the proband.
Influx of glucose was impaired but efflux of glucose from the mucosa of these three heterozygotes was identical with that in three normal controls.
A kinetic analysis indicated a reduced capacity (V(max)), but a normal affinity (K(m)) for glucose transport by their intestinal mucosa.

findings.statement: Elsas et al. (1970) concluded that familial glucose-galactose malabsorption is inherited as an autosomal recessive trait. They also concluded that heterozygotes are detectable because their capacity for glucose transport is reduced.
quotes: We conclude that familial glucose-galactose malabsorption is inherited as an autosomal recessive trait, that heterozygotes for this disorder are detectable and demonstrate a reduced capacity for glucose transport

findings.statement: Elsas et al. (1970) concluded that the absence of intestinal glucose transport in glucose-galactose malabsorption is accompanied by partial impairment of renal glucose transport. The proband's brother had a renal titration curve similar to those of 7 normal volunteers.
quotes: absent intestinal glucose transport is accompanied by partial impairment of renal glucose transport.
Her brother's titration curve was similar to that of seven normal volunteers.

relevance_reason: First identification of an SGLT1 missense mutation causing GGM in a family, with functional evidence in Xenopus oocytes.

findings.statement: Turk et al. (1991) described glucose/galactose malabsorption as an autosomal recessive disease that manifests within the first weeks of life and is characterized by a selective failure to absorb dietary glucose and galactose from the intestine. The resulting severe diarrhea and dehydration are usually fatal unless these sugars are removed from the diet.
quotes: Glucose/galactose malabsorption (GGM) is an autosomal recessive disease manifesting within the first weeks of life and characterized by a selective failure to absorb dietary glucose and galactose from the intestine.
The consequent severe diarrhoea and dehydration are usually fatal unless these sugars are eliminated from the diet.

findings.statement: Turk et al. (1991) noted that the severe diarrhea and dehydration of GGM are usually fatal unless glucose and galactose are eliminated from the diet.
quotes: The consequent severe diarrhoea and dehydration are usually fatal unless these sugars are eliminated from the diet.

findings.statement: Turk et al. (1991) noted that intestinal biopsies from GGM patients had shown a specific defect in Na(+)-dependent glucose absorption in the brush border. Normal absorption is mediated by the Na+/glucose cotransporter in the brush border membrane, which is encoded by SGLT1 on distal chromosome 22q.
quotes: Intestinal biopsies of GGM patients have revealed a specific defect in Na(+)-dependent absorption of glucose in the brush border.
We have previously cloned and sequenced a Na+/glucose cotransporter from normal human ileum and shown that this gene, SGLT1, resides on the distal q arm of chromosome 22.

findings.statement: In members of a family with GGM, Turk et al. (1991) used PCR to amplify SGLT1 cDNA and genomic DNA and found a single missense mutation in SGLT1 that cosegregated with the GGM phenotype. In Xenopus oocytes injected with cRNA carrying the mutation, Na(+)-dependent glucose transport was completely lost.
quotes: We have now amplified SGLT1 complementary DNA and genomic DNA from members of a family affected with GGM by the polymerase chain reaction.

Sequence analysis of the amplified products has revealed a single missense mutation in SGLT1 which cosegregates with the GGM phenotype and results in a complete loss of Na(+)-dependent glucose transport in Xenopus oocytes injected with this complementary RNA.
